title: `sizeof(*v)` operands keep the array allocation itself refused: 224 leaves on 211 Unknown functions, 4 sole-blocked
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS makes a heap array `T **v` a collection only once `v` is bound to the identity its allocation produced, and the corpus spells that allocation `v = malloc(n * sizeof(*v))` or `sizeof *v`. The lexical access gate (`contains_unmodeled_access`) reads the `*` after `sizeof` or `(` as a dereference, and the fixed type-query rule (type_query.rs) admits only a scalar type name or a declared scalar local, so the statement is refused as `indirect memory access` and `v` never binds (rd_kafka_mock_sharegroup_get_member_ids, rd_kafka_ListGroups_resp_cb, ut_tq_test). Measured at the base census (docs/reports/w43-indexed-resource-collections/census/census.txt, section sizeof_dereference_operand): 224 `indirect memory access` leaves in 211 Unknown functions whose only access on the line is such an operand, 4 of them sole-blocked; the shape is far wider than collections (`ctx = flb_calloc(1, sizeof(*ctx))`). C11 6.5.3.4p2 leaves a non-VLA operand unevaluated. DISCHARGE: a type-query card admitting `sizeof(*NAME)`/`sizeof *NAME` for a declared object pointer whose pointee is not a variably modified type, with its VLA argument, Lean parity and a measured re-pin; W43-RETURN-TYPE-OPERATOR is its return-position neighbour.

title: An element store from a named pointer (`v[i] = p`) stays refused
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS admits an element store only when its value is an acquiring contract call (every parameter borrowed, an owned result) or the null constant. After `v[i] = p` the name `p` would remain an alias of an element whose custody the collection now holds: a later release through `p` would be a second release the ranges do not see, and a later borrow of `p` after the element's release a use after release the projection could not report, because an unknown binding is admitted at a borrowed position. The card therefore keeps the refusal byte for byte (test `storing_a_named_pointer_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`). The base census counts 57 `NAME[...] = NAME` stores in 42 functions (36 Unknown), 4 of them from a name an acquiring call bound; it reads source tokens and does not separate pointer-to-pointer bases from scalar arrays. DISCHARGE: a rule that retires the stored name's binding into a refusal-bearing state (every later use refuses) or proves it dead, with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: Only the canonical counted `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` carries an exit equation; the corpus fills by append over traversals and releases with `while (i-- > 0)`
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS recognises a counted loop only as `for (I = 0; I < B; I++)` around at least one lowered element operation, with `I` and `B` declared integers no other lvalue designates, no write of either in the body, no `break`/`goto`/label/`switch`, and an unsigned index no narrower than an unsigned bound. The append `v[n++] = ACQUIRE(...)` needs no loop recognition and is admitted in any loop. The base census found 20 loops around element stores or releases: 9 fill loops (1 canonical; the rest append over pointer or list traversals, which W43-INDEX-TRAVERSAL owns), 11 release loops (9 canonical), 0 partial-cleanup loops, 2 `while` loops (`while (i-- > 0) rd_free(grps[i]);`), and 6 non-canonical `for` loops (a member bound `args->qcnt`, a narrower unsigned index against a `size_t` bound in rd_kafka_conf_dump_free). Reconciled with W43-INDEX-TRAVERSAL on the merged tree (merge eea0b30b): traversal adds no separate fixpoint (the existing work list reaches the loop's fixed point), and the only fact both state is a declared scalar's zero. Traversal keeps it as a target-free binding in the custody pointer map, joined by the custody join, where any joining path lacking it drops it; this card keeps it in a collection-only set whose join ignores a path that is vacuous for the collection (a counted loop's body edge under a bound that is zero when clamped). Reading traversal's fact instead was measured: 5 of the 32 collection tests regress, the brief's fill-with-partial-cleanup among them, because the partial cleanup's first-iteration body edge is vacuous and its stepped index would erase the entry zero at the cleanup header. The body-edge `i < n` fact, the clamped zero, the exit equation `i = max(0, n)` and the vacuous edge have no traversal counterpart (traversal evaluates no bound). Both cards forget an index stepped in a subscript (`v[n++]`, `B[X++]`). DISCHARGE: a decrementing release sweep, `while` headers and member bounds read under their own premises, and the zero fact made vacuity-aware in the shared custody map so the collection-only copy can be deleted, each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: No contract or summary mode states "an owned array of owned elements": destroy helpers over a caller's array stay Unknown and a returned collection publishes no summary
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS decides collections this body acquired. A helper that releases a caller's array (`destroy_prometheus_label_list`, `destroy_prometheus_sample_list`, `free_metrics`, `free_resource_attributes`, `rd_kafka_conf_dump_free`, and cmetrics' seven `destroy_*_list` NULL-assigning loops) has an unbound formal base, so every element operation keeps its refusal byte for byte; and a body that returns a filled collection is itself Safe but its exit is observed as `Ambiguous`, because a one-identity `Owned` summary would let a caller free the array and leak its elements (test `a_helper_returning_a_filled_collection_publishes_no_summary`). Resource vocabulary version 1 has no clause for element custody. DISCHARGE: a contract/summary clause for a collection result and a collection release (`resource_released_elements(p, n)` or similar) with loader, gateway, W4 validation and Lean parity, measured on the corpus.

title: Automatic arrays of owned pointers (`T *a[N]`) and descriptor arrays (`int fds[N]`) are not collection owners
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS keys a collection by the heap identity of a `T **` base. An automatic array has no identity, its lifetime is the frame's, and it decays to a pointer a callee can reach whenever it is named without a subscript; `ut_tq_test`'s `struct ut_tq_head *tqh[3] = {NULL, …}` is the corpus witness (its braced initializer is refused as well). Descriptor, stream and directory elements are refused. On the merged tree with W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING (merge eea0b30b) a collection's owner, every element's acquisition and every discharging release must be of heap kind, a statement reading a tracked descriptor keeps its refusal, and all five element and loop instruction variants are refused by `admits_descriptor_read` (tests `a_stream_element_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`, `a_stream_release_of_a_heap_element_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`; Lean `only_heap_elements_are_collected`). A kind-indexed collection is not cheap: descriptor arrays are `int *fds` or `int fds[N]`, whose elements are integers (the `T **` premise, the null-test refinement and the null-constant store do not apply; validity is a `-1` sentinel), and a kind mismatch on an element would need its own settled-state accusation. At this card's census no descriptor release was contracted; W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING has since declared `close`. DISCHARGE: an automatic-array owner with its lifetime and decay premises, and kind-indexed elements (integer-carried descriptor collections with sentinel validity, stream and directory elements with kind-matched releases), each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: The element leak, element double release and element use-after-release arms reach no function of the pinned corpus
why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS proves and unit-tests its accusing arms (tests `freeing_the_array_with_live_elements_is_an_element_leak`, `a_partial_cleanup_that_frees_only_the_array_leaks_the_prefix`, `releasing_an_element_twice_is_a_double_release`, `a_second_release_loop_is_a_double_release`, `testing_a_released_element_is_a_use_after_release`, `an_element_operation_through_a_released_array_is_a_use_after_release`, `overwriting_a_live_element_is_a_leak`; Lean QCore.IndexedCollection). At its arbiter no element operation's array resolved in any corpus function, so the AFTER diagnostics are byte-identical to BEFORE apart from the report's `scope` string, and the unchanged leak pin (271) records that absence rather than the arms' verification. DISCHARGE: the first arbiter in which an element operation's array resolves (most likely after W43-COLLECTION-SIZEOF-DEREFERENCE-ALLOCATION) attributes every element leaf it adds or removes, with a witness for each violation candidate.

title: An element node carries its refusal as a fallback, so the certificate firewall does not see an unreached one as a retained `Unknown`
why: check_legacy_safety_certificate rejects any function whose CFG retains a `LegacyInstruction::Unknown` node, even one the abstract semantics never reaches. Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS lowers an element store, release or null test to its own instruction carrying the classifier's refusal as `fallback`; the fallback applies (byte for byte) whenever the array does not resolve in the reaching state, and a node no state reaches applies nothing. The card treats an element node like any other modelled instruction (an unreached one raises nothing) rather than like a retained refusal, deliberately: counting it as `Unknown` would reject every Safe collection body. The difference from the firewall's stated caution is therefore real on a path the analysis pruned. DISCHARGE: a recorded decision that an unreached modelled element node needs no containment, or a firewall rule that rejects an element node with no settled incoming state, with the corpus re-measured.
